answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, slashable stake rather than its claimed identity. An agent locks copper-denominated deposits behind an anchor credential; peers can challenge suspicious behavior, and a verified duplicate or coordinated fraud causes the stake to be forfeited. Splitting into a grove of fake accounts then multiplies the capital at risk, while earning influence still requires time and consistent service. This raises the cost of Sybils without pretending identity checks alone can eliminate them.
